transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-20
Time: 11:00 AM PT
Duration: ~38 minutes
Attendees: Alex Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Mark Holloway (CTO - Northern Insurance), Sara Lin (Eng Mgr), Derek Ramos (SRE)

Summary (auto): quick hosted API walkthrough focused on chat/text generation basics: streaming, params, retries. Discussed security questions (SOC2, SSO), latency vs cost tradeoffs, and next steps for a short POC.

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex: hey everyone, thanks for joining. alex from redwood inference here, i'll hand it over to priya to do a quick demo, but first just quick intros?
[00:12] Mark: hi mark holloway, cto at northern insurance. we're looking at LLMs for customer support automation and claims triage, want to understand latency and cost trade offs.
[00:20] Sara: sara, eng manager, i'll own integration. we've got some compliance constraints around data residency.
[00:26] Derek: derek, sre, curious about retries/backoff and circuit breaker behaviour.
[00:34] Priya: great, thanks. i'll share my screen, demo will be hosted api chat + text generation basics — streaming, params like temperature/top_p/max_tokens, and retry semantics.
[00:45] Priya: first, quick product overview: redwood api — simple rest and sdk, chat endpoint supports streaming, function/tool calling, structured output. (note: sometimes the transcript shows "redwood apee" but it's redwood api).
[00:58] Priya: i'll start with a basic chat example. here's a prompt, we'll call the chat endpoint with model "redwood-alpha-1" (demo model name), temperature .2, max_tokens 300.
[01:12] Priya: streaming: you can stream partial tokens back to reduce perceived latency. you see the response arriving token by token in the ui. we also support server-sent events and grpc streaming for higher throughput.
[01:30] Sara: is streaming reliable for short messages? we worry about partial renders and ordering.
[01:36] Priya: yep — streaming is deterministic for a single request; ordering issues only happen if you multiplex on the client. also you can set the response completion policy so you only render final paragraphs if that suits you.
[01:48] Mark: how do we control cost — say we need sub-200ms p95 for short messages, what's the usual levers?
[01:55] Priya: latency vs cost — main controls are model selection (smaller model cheaper/faster), batching and concurrency settings, prefix caching for common prompts, and request params like max_tokens and stopping sequences. we also recommend quantized model variants for self-hosted/dedicated but hosted api has optimized kernels.
[02:20] Alex: also FYI we have an "optimize" recommendations tab in the console that suggests batching and quantization profiles based on observed traffic.
[02:32] Derek: do you expose per-token cost and latency breakdowns? we need that for SRE budgets.
[02:38] Alex: yeah console shows token-level cost, per-route latency heatmaps, and tracing hooks. you can export the data.
[02:45] Priya: moving on to params: temperature 0-1, top_p, repetition penalty, stop sequences and max tokens. for customer support we usually recommend temperature 0-0.3 and a top_p around .8 for safer responses.
[03:05] Mark: what about deterministic outputs for templates? we need the model to not hallucinate policy numbers.
[03:11] Priya: for deterministic use, use lower temperature and you can pin model versions; also use function calling or structured output to force constrained formats. we can also do a fine-tune or prompt engineering and validation layer.
[03:30] Derek: retry behavior — if the request 5xxs or times out, what happens client-side?
[03:36] Priya: hosted api returns standard http 5xx / 429 codes. we recommend exponential backoff with jitter. for idempotency we include request ids so you can detect duplicates; for streaming requests we recommend a restart semantics in the client. our sdk has built-in retry helper with configurable max attempts and backoff policy.
[03:58] Sara: and rate limits? we have bursty traffic during business hours.
[04:03] Alex: hosted api has per-account rate limits and you can request quota increases. for production at scale we often recommend dedicated capacity, which gives reserved GPUs and configurable autoscaling.
[04:18] Mark: if we do hosted, is customer data stored? we're subject to data retention rules.
[04:23] Alex: by default hosted retains logs for X days but you can opt out; we also offer private deployments with a customer-managed control plane for strict residency. all options integrate with KMS for envelope encryption. note: transcript shows "KMS/HSM" sometimes as "KM S H M".
[04:42] Priya: demo — i'll send a couple of simulated customer queries. first one: "Summarize claim: vehicle collision — what are the next steps for the customer?"
[04:54] [Demo typing noises]
[05:02] Priya: streaming response starting... "First, ensure safety..." (response streams in) you can see partial sentences as they arrive. end result is a structured list.
[05:20] Sara: nice. how do you handle sensitive PII in prompts? we need redaction before logs.
[05:27] Priya: options: client-side redaction before sending, and server-side redaction hooks; we also have tokenization filters and ML-based PII detection. for audit we can provide end-to-end logs with redaction markers.
[05:42] Derek: network-wise, do we have region control? we need EU residency for some data.
[05:47] Alex: yes, hosted regions include NA and EU, and Private deployments can run in your VPC. for on-prem we have an appliance option.
[05:58] Mark: curious about p95 numbers — what can you deliver on hosted for a short prompt?
[06:04] Priya: depends on model: for smaller chat-optimized models you can see p95 in ~90-180ms for short prompts; larger models are higher. we have perf profiles in the model catalog. again these are approximations because sequence length and concurrency change numbers.
[06:24] Mark: can you run a quick benchmark with our sample payloads?
[06:28] Priya: yes, that's typical next step — we'll run a short POC benchmark on our hosted env or on dedicated nodes if you prefer. we'll need sample prompts and QPS targets.
[06:40] Alex: i'll follow up with a checklist and invitation to a benchmark run.
[06:47] Mark: ok. other technical concerns: telemetry and tracing — we need correlation IDs through our stack.
[06:53] Priya: we emit request ids and have tracing hooks that integrate with opentelemetry; you can link traces to your logs.
[07:05] Sara: error modes — what do clients see on partial failure during streaming?
[07:09] Priya: streaming can be resumed if you save the last token index; otherwise you'll see an http disconnect and a 5xx if server fails. for robustness we recommend client-side buffering and replay semantics.
[07:24] Derek: anything about caching? we have a lot of templated replies.
[07:28] Priya: prefix or KV caching — we can cache the KV cache for continuations to dramatically reduce compute for similar conversations; for templated responses you can do deterministic template rendering at the app layer and only call LLM for slots.
[07:44] Mark: security/compliance — SOC2? pen tests?
[07:48] Alex: yes we are SOC 2 Type II, have an ISO roadmap and can share the security pack. we do yearly pen tests and can share redacted reports under NDA.
[07:59] Sara: SSO / SCIM for user management?
[08:03] Alex: support for SAML/SSO and SCIM provisioning; RBAC and audit logs in the console.
[08:12] Priya: back to demo — i'll show retry behavior by forcing a timeout in the client. (demo shows sdk code) example: sdk.chat.create({model: 'redwood-alpha-1', input: ..., timeoutMs: 1000, retry: {maxAttempts:3, backoff: 'exponential'}})
[08:34] [Demo: small code snippet displayed]
[08:40] Priya: for streaming we use an event stream so client can reconnect with resume token; small interruptions rarely cause duplicate tokens but client should dedupe by request id.
[08:55] Derek: congrats, that's helpful. what's the SLA for hosted?
[09:00] Alex: hosted has best-effort SLAs; Dedicated gives SLA-backed uptime and latency commitments. Private/On-Prem gets you full control but is licensed differently.
[09:13] Mark: how quickly can we ramp to 100 RPS for short prompts in a pilot?
[09:18] Priya: for hosted, request a quota increase — we can provision burst capacity. for predictable throughput we recommend Dedicated which you can reserve. POC typically runs within 1-2 weeks to validate latency and cost.
[09:33] Sara: anything about model rollouts? we need to A/B test a new prompt set.
[09:37] Alex: we have rollouts in console: canary, A/B, automatic fallback policies to older model variants.
[09:45] Mark: what about observability for guardrails — can we get diffs when model outputs degrade?
[09:51] Priya: yes, optimize includes quality monitoring and regression alerts tied to prompt sets and evals; you can set a regression threshold to trigger a rollback.
[10:06] [Longer demo segment — showing console optimize tab, model catalog, and streaming example]
[12:20] Priya: quick note — some transcripts show terms wrong, like "KV cash" instead of KV cache; just ignore those small typos in the auto transcript.
[12:31] Derek: cost question — can you give an example cost calc for 1M short messages/month?
[12:36] Alex: rough calc: per-token cost times avg tokens per request; for short 20-token responses and 10-token prompts that's ~30 tokens/request. multiply by 1M = 30M tokens. cost depends on model; we'll send an example sheet.
[12:58] Mark: do you support role-based prompt templates or team-wide prompt library?
[13:04] Priya: console has prompt library and you can share templates across teams with permissions.
[13:12] Sara: any gotchas with streaming on mobile clients?
[13:16] Priya: mobile is fine, just watch connection handoffs and reconnection; use resume tokens.
[13:25] Mark: are there any limitations on function calling payload size?
[13:29] Priya: function args are limited by max tokens; for large structured outputs we recommend chunking or using attachments via a document store.
[13:42] Derek: do you have examples of integrating with our ticketing system?
[13:46] Alex: we've done integrations with zendesk, jira, and custom webhooks; can share reference apps.
[13:55] Priya: demo end — quick recap: streaming reduces perceived latency, params tune cost/creativity, use retry/backoff and idempotency for robustness, use optimize recommendations for batching/caching.
[14:12] Mark: next steps — we'd like pricing, security docs, and a POC.
[14:18] Alex: noted. we'll send pricing and security pack, plus a checklist for the POC. priya will run the benchmark.
[14:25] Sara: timeline — we want pilot in the next month if possible.
[14:29] Priya: that's doable, schedule dependent.
[14:32] Derek: last question: can you do a dedicated eval of p95 under our workload?
[14:36] Alex: yes — if you want guaranteed numbers use Dedicated; we can run hosted pilot first and then move to dedicated if you need SLAs.
[14:45] Mark: okay thanks, that answers most.
[14:48] Alex: great — i'll follow up by end of tomorrow with docs and next steps.
[14:53] Meeting end / small misc wrap-up.
